name: publicWeb_savePageLayout
description: Saves (inserts or updates) the Puck page layout JSON blob for a kennel. Validates that the JSON is well-formed via ISJSON(). If no KennelWebsite row exists yet, inserts a minimal one with Enabled=0 so saving a layout does not auto-publish the website. Called by the Next.js admin layout editor via the PublicWebAdminApi POST endpoint.

parameters.name: KennelSlug
parameters.description: URL slug of the kennel whose layout to save

parameters.name: PageLayoutJson
parameters.description: JSON blob of shape PageLayoutBlob = Partial<Record<PageType, Data>>. Must pass SQL Server ISJSON() validation.

columns.name: ErrorMessage
columns.description: NULL on success; error description on failure

sideEffects: Updates HC.KennelWebsite.PageLayoutJson and updatedAt for the resolved kennel
Inserts a minimal HC.KennelWebsite row (KennelId, PageLayoutJson, Enabled=0) if none exists

codeSmells.issue: Auto-insert of KennelWebsite row on save
codeSmells.detail: If no KennelWebsite row exists, the SP inserts a minimal one with Enabled=0. This is intentional and documented in the SP comment. However, two concurrent first-time saves could produce a primary key violation on the second INSERT. Same race as hcportal_getKennelWebsite — low probability but worth noting.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove the Success/ErrorMessage columns — the Next.js route checks Success to show toast feedback
Never change the Enabled=0 default on auto-insert — the admin must explicitly enable the website separately
Never remove the ISJSON() check — it prevents corrupted blobs reaching the DB
